blocks.content: Docker Hub is the default public registry that Docker points to out of the box. Unless you specify otherwise, every docker pull and docker push talks to Docker Hub.

When you run docker pull nginx without specifying a registry hostname, Docker assumes you mean Docker Hub, and fetches the nginx repository from there. This default is convenient for getting started, but worth knowing explicitly, since it is easy to assume an image came from "the internet" generically when it specifically came from Hub.

blocks.alt: No registry specified means Docker Hub by default

blocks.content: Docker Hub hosts two very different kinds of content. Official images (like nginx, postgres, node) are curated and maintained by Docker and the upstream project teams, reviewed for security and best practices. Anyone can also publish their own images under a username or organization, with far less guarantee about quality or maintenance.

blocks.alt: Official images are curated, user images vary widely

blocks.content:
docker pull nginx          # official image
docker pull bitnami/nginx  # a specific publisher's image

docker pull bitnami/nginx  # a specific publisher's image

blocks.content: 3. What Actually Happens on a Pull
blocks.text: 3. What Actually Happens on a Pull

blocks.content: A docker pull against Docker Hub looks up the requested repository and tag, then downloads each image layer that is not already cached locally. Layers are covered in depth in the Docker Images module, the important part here is that Hub only needs to send layers you do not already have.

blocks.alt: Only missing layers are actually downloaded

blocks.content: 4. Rate Limits Are a Real Production Gotcha
blocks.text: 4. Rate Limits Are a Real Production Gotcha

blocks.content: Docker Hub rate-limits pulls per IP address for anonymous (not logged in) users, and at a higher but still real limit for free authenticated accounts. Teams running CI pipelines that pull frequently from a shared IP have genuinely been blocked mid-deploy by this, it is a common enough incident that it is worth knowing about before it surprises you.

blocks.alt: Authenticating raises the limit, it does not remove it

blocks.content:
docker login
# Authenticating before pulling in CI raises your rate limit
# significantly compared to anonymous pulls.

# significantly compared to anonymous pulls.

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Docker Hub is the default registry, any pull or push without an explicit registry hostname goes there.
Official images are curated and reviewed, user-published images are not, know which one you are pulling.
Anonymous pull rate limits are a real production concern, authenticating (or using a private mirror) is the standard fix.
